claims.text: FeNiCoCrMo0.5Al1.3 powder can be deposited by HVOF spraying.
In-flight oxidation during HVOF affects the phase composition and properties of FeNiCoCrMo0.5Al1.3 coatings.
An inert shielding gas during HVOF will finely control or moderate in-flight oxidation.
Rapid heating and cooling during HVOF allow oxidation and phase formation before complete decomposition of the supersaturated solid solution.
Increasing or controlling spraying distance changes the extent of oxidation, including the amount of alpha-Al2O3.
Isothermal annealing at 800 °C produces phase transformations and elemental redistribution in FeNiCoCrMo0.5Al1.3.
During annealing at 800 °C, the supersaturated BCC solid solution decomposes with sigma-phase formation and diffusion of Al, Cr, Fe, and Mo toward the surface.
The sprayed coating will retain or form a supersaturated BCC structure.
HVOF oxidation causes aluminum diffusion to the particle surface, surface Al2O3 formation, and FCC formation in the aluminum-depleted subsurface layer.
Annealing produces a compact, fine-scale oxide network at the coating surface.
The surface oxide network acts as an effective oxygen-diffusion barrier.
Annealing refines the coating into a hard, oxidation-resistant microstructure.
The proposed coating will reduce oxygen penetration and oxidation-induced weight gain on zirconium-alloy cladding.
The proposed coating will reduce oxide-scale spallation and preserve mechanical integrity during high-temperature oxidation.
Bare or conventionally coated zirconium-alloy cladding exhibits greater oxidation weight gain and scale spallation than the proposed coating under identical conditions.
Insufficient inert-gas flow or an improper annealing temperature will diminish coating effectiveness.
Oxidation performance can be compared using weight gain per unit area, oxide morphology, phase analysis, coating integrity, and microhardness.
Failure to obtain a statistically significant reduction in oxidation weight gain or a uniform dense oxide layer relative to the control would falsify the hypothesis.
